places.name_en: Eradah Complex and Mental Health, Riyadh
places.operator_en: Ministry of Health - Riyadh Third Health Cluster
places.address_en: New headquarters at Exit 18 on An Nahdah Road, Riyadh
places.hours_note_en: Emergency department runs around the clock. All other services: Sunday to Thursday 08:00-16:00 (cluster statement, Feb 2026).
places.access_note_en: Emergency is open 24 hours. MoH describes the Eradah complexes as specialised facilities giving free treatment for psychiatric illness and for addiction. MoH addiction pathway (2023 guide): call 937, anonymously if wished; doctors triage the call and book a direct appointment in an addiction clinic at a general or psychiatric hospital, or arrange admission when needed.
places.notes: MOVED: Riyadh Third Health Cluster said the complex left its Al Khuzama site and began operating at the new headquarters on 13 Feb 2026. New-site coordinates could not be confirmed (nothing in OpenStreetMap or Nominatim yet), so lat/lng are null. general_notes.topic: Source and date of the urgent care list
general_notes.text_en: All 24 urgent_care entries come from the Ministry of Health page 'On-Duty Healthcare Centers - Riyadh'. The Arabic page was last modified 8 Dhu al-Hijjah 1447 AH (about 25 May 2026); the English page on 9 May 2026. The table has four hour columns: Sunday-Thursday 8am-11pm, Sunday-Thursday 24 hours, all week 8am-11pm, all week 24 hours. Only the first table (Riyadh city) was used; the second table (governorates such as Al-Kharj, Al-Muzahimiyah, Al-Majmaah, Dawadmi) is outside the metro area and was left out.

general_notes.topic: Arabic and English MoH lists disagree
general_notes.text_en: The two language versions differ. Arabic (newer, used as primary) adds Ad Dar Al Baida Second, An Nadwah, Al Yasmin and Abdulmunim Al Rashed, and shows Al Ghadeer, King Faisal and Al Sahafa as open all week; the English page shows those three as Sunday-Thursday only. The English page also lists 'Diriyah Healthcare Center' (Third Cluster, all week 8am-11pm; link resolves to 'Prince Sultan ibn Abdulaziz Primary Health Center' at about 24.74788, 46.56935), which is absent from the Arabic page and so was not added as a place. Only four centres are marked 24 hours: As Sulaymaniyah, Al Wadi, Al Manar and Laban Al Sharqi.

MoH does not publish direct phone numbers for the on-duty primary healthcare centres. The MoH unified number is 937. It does not fit the +966 / 9200 phone format requested, so the phone field is null for those entries.

general_notes.topic: Urgent care centres as a named service
general_notes.text_en: Riyadh First Health Cluster reported 108,734 visits to its 'urgent care centres' (مراكز الرعاية العاجلة) in the first half of 2026, so the service exists under that name, but no public list of which centres carry it was found beyond the MoH on-duty table. An older MoH statement (March 2020) said Riyadh city had 19 on-duty centres, 17 open 16 hours a day and 2 open 24 hours.

MoH (Riyadh Health Affairs, March 2020) said the aim of extended-hours centres run on the urgent care model is to ease pressure on hospital emergency departments and make primary care easier to reach.

general_notes.topic: Who runs dialysis for MoH patients
general_notes.text_en: MoH buys a large share of dialysis from two contracted companies, DaVita and Diaverum. The MoH renal care programme guide (2023) counts about 1.3 million haemodialysis sessions a year in MoH-run centres and about 1.1 million in the companies' centres, and names DaVita and Diaverum as the contracted companies. In Riyadh city that means three DaVita and three Diaverum clinics, two of them inside MoH hospitals.

general_notes.topic: King Abdullah Foundation dialysis centres (not listed)
general_notes.text_en: The National Guard Health Affairs site says two charity dialysis centres of the King Abdullah International Foundation for Humanitarian Works operate in Riyadh (north and south branches) with NGHA operational support. No address, name, phone or current status could be found, so they are NOT in the places list. They need a follow-up with NGHA.

general_notes.topic: Kellana charity (support, not a dialysis centre)
general_notes.text_en: The Prince Fahd bin Salman Charity Association for Renal Failure Patients Care (Kellana) is based in Al Malqa, Riyadh (phones on its site: 0114103332 and 0542025060). Its programmes include haemodialysis care for kidney failure patients, kidney transplant support, medicines and a transport allowance. It funds care rather than running a walk-in dialysis centre, so it is not in the places list.

Riyadh Third Health Cluster moved the Eradah Complex and Mental Health from Al Khuzama district to a new headquarters at Exit 18 on An Nahdah Road; the new site started operating on 13 February 2026. Emergency runs 24 hours; other services Sunday to Thursday 8am-4pm. Older maps, the MoH 2023 guide link and OpenStreetMap still show the old site.

general_notes.topic: How MoH routes addiction and mental health cases
general_notes.text_en: The MoH guide to addiction treatment and rehabilitation services (first edition, 2023) says access is through the 937 call centre (callers may stay anonymous) or the Sehhaty app's instant consultations; stable cases get a direct appointment in an addiction clinic at a general or psychiatric hospital, unstable cases are coordinated for admission, and dangerous cases go to 911. It also lists a national addiction consultation line, 1955. Helplines themselves are covered by another researcher; this note only explains why several entries say 'via 937'.

general_notes.topic: MoH list of mental health hospitals
general_notes.text_en: MoH's list of mental health complexes and hospitals (2021) has a single entry for Riyadh city: Eradah Complex and Mental Health in Riyadh. The nearest other one is in Al-Kharj, outside the metro area.

Urgent care and most mental health coordinates were read from the Google Maps short links published on MoH pages and in the MoH guide (each link was opened and the place coordinates taken from the resolved address). DaVita and Diaverum coordinates are the latitude and longitude published in their own site data. Two entries use OpenStreetMap (King Salman Center for Kidney Diseases, node 11871539496; Al Yasmin health centre, way 1301681280). District names come from Nominatim reverse geocoding unless a note says otherwise. Every non-null coordinate is inside lat 24.3-25.2, lng 46.3-47.1. OpenStreetMap itself has almost no dialysis or mental health features tagged in Riyadh.

general_notes.topic: Names in the brief that could not be matched
general_notes.text_en: No dialysis centre named 'Prince Abdulrahman Al Faisal centre' was found. The nearest match is the DaVita clinic at Imam Abdulrahman Al Faisal Hospital. 'Prince Salman kidney centre' is the old name of King Salman Center for Kidney Diseases.
